en.headline: Development chief stresses ecology and heritage in Northern Metropolis
en.dek: Bernadette Linn said the government would balance growth with the area's history and natural resources, naming a San Tin trail as next year's first rural-urban integration project.
body: Development Bureau chief Bernadette Linn said the government was committed to making the Northern Metropolis a new growth engine while valuing its ecology, historic buildings and culture.

Speaking at the opening of the Hong Kong Culture and Sustainable Development Conference 2026, she said the area's traditional villages and natural resources gave the development a distinctive character, and that rural-urban integration was a key focus.

She identified the San Tin Time Trail as the first major rural-urban integration project to be launched next year. It will link buildings with rural traditional features and other historical and cultural sites.

The government has also set up a 200-million-dollar Northern Metropolis Rural-Urban Integration Fund to support community-led work such as revitalising traditional village buildings, showcasing rural cultural activities and telling village stories. Linn said the same approach applied to heritage conservation across Hong Kong through the Revitalising Historic Buildings Through Partnership Scheme.

zh.headline: 甧漢豪：北都發展珍視生態歷史文化 推動城鄉共融
zh.dek: 發展局局長稱政府明年推出「新田時光步道」作為首個重點城鄉共融項目，並已成立兩億元基金支持社區主導計劃。
body: 發展局局長甧漢豪表示，政府致力將北部都會區發展成香港新增長引擎，同時珍視當地生態、歷史文物和文化，倡導平衡發展。
她在「香港文化與可持續發展會議2026」開幕典禮致辭時說，北都豐富的歷史、傳統鄉鎮和自然資源為發展增添獨特氣息，推動城鄉共融是其中一個重點。
甧漢豪指，政府明年推出的首個重點城鄉共融項目「新田時光步道」，將把富有鄉村傳統特色的建築和歷史文化景點串連起來。
除政府牽頭項目外，當局已宣布成立兩億元「北都城鄉共融基金」，支持活化傳統鄉村建築、展示鄉村文化活動及講述鄉村故事等社區主導項目。她又說，同樣原則適用於全港歷史建築保育，政府透過活化歷史建築伙伴計劃與非牟利機構合作。
